title: Soil Organic Carbon
content: Soil organic carbon is an important indicator of soil condition and contributes to soil structure, nutrient cycling and biological activity.

title: Soil Moisture
content: Soil moisture affects plant growth and soil biological processes. It is influenced by rainfall, soil properties and land management.

title: Rainfall
content: Rainfall and water availability influence plant growth, ecosystem processes and habitat conditions. Changes in water availability can affect organisms and ecosystem functioning.

title: Species Richness
content: Species richness describes the number of different species present in an ecological area and can be used as one indicator of biodiversity.

title: Habitat Diversity
content: Greater habitat diversity can provide different resources and conditions for organisms and can support biodiversity.

title: Crop Diversity
content: Increasing diversity within agricultural systems can provide a greater variety of habitats and resources compared with simplified agricultural systems.

title: Agroforestry
content: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or other agricultural activities. Such systems can provide additional habitat and ecosystem functions.

title: Deforestation
content: Loss of forest habitat can reduce available habitat for species and can contribute to changes in ecosystem structure and biodiversity.

title: Pollution
content: Pollution can place pressure on ecosystems and organisms. Effects depend on the pollutant, concentration, exposure and ecosystem involved.
